title: Assessment of Tariff-impact on Singapore's Trade Sectors following US' Section 301 Investigations
what_it_is: Assessment of Tariff-impact on Singapore's Trade Sectors following US' Section 301 Investigations

sections.label: US Section 301 investigations initiated
sections.summary: On 11 and 12 March 2026, the Office of the US Trade Representative initiated two investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On 11 and 12 March 2026, the Office of the US Trade Representative initiated two investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

sections.label: Singapore US trade surplus dispute
sections.summary: A US notice said Singapore had a US$27 billion bilateral trade surplus with the US in 2024, but MTI clarified the US ran that surplus.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The US Trade Representative's Federal Register Notice on the investigation into structural excess capacity had highlighted that Singapore enjoyed a bilateral trade surplus with the US in both goods and services amounting to US$27 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has clarified that it was the US which ran a trade surplus of US$27 billion with Singapore in 2024.

sections.label: Section 122 tariff on Singapore exports
sections.summary: The Section 122 tariff of 10% imposed on Singapore's exports to the US since 24 February 2026 remains unchanged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: In the meantime, the Section 122 tariff of 10% imposed on Singapore's exports to the US since 24 February 2026 remains unchanged.

sections.label: US reasons for including Singapore
sections.summary: The US has not given reasons for including Singapore under the Section 301 investigations, and it is unknown if other countries share a similar perspective.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: To the first and also the third question, the US has not given us reasons on why they have included Singapore under the Section 301 investigations and neither do we know if other countries might have similar perspective.

sections.label: Advice to affected companies premature
sections.summary: It is premature to give meaningful and useful advice to companies that may potentially be affected by the Section 301 investigations.

sentences.text: And how are we supporting them, possibly in the future, in navigating these complexities?

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: It is actually premature for us to give any meaningful and useful advice to companies that may potentially be affected by the Section 301 investigations.

sections.label: Contact and Business Adaptation Grant
sections.summary: They have been kept in touch with, and a Business Adaptation Grant remains available to help companies understand the US tariffs' implications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We have been keeping in touch with them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Also, there is a Business Adaptation Grant, which remains available to help companies understand the implications of the US tariffs on their businesses.

sections.label: Attending the hearings
sections.summary: The answer is yes, and they will be attending the hearings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The answer is yes; we will be attending the hearings.
